name: xDSL
staging_note: Normal-sized pure-Python repository, staged as a full shallow clone (`git clone --depth 1`), matching this repo's flat donor-staging convention (donor root = repo root, no extra repo-name nesting). Nested `.git` metadata removed after capturing the pinned commit SHA.
pin_policy: This exact commit SHA is the durable pin. The clone was a floating shallow clone of xdsl's HEAD at clone time (depth 1); the SHA recorded here, not any branch name, is the identity that must be used to re-derive or re-verify this donor's content.
license_evidence: Verified by reading .atlas/temporary/donors/xdsl/LICENSE directly: header text reads 'The xDSL project is under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions'. Cross-checked against pyproject.toml's `project.license` field: {text = "Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions"}.
relationship_to_mlir_donor: xDSL is a from-scratch pure-Python reimplementation of MLIR's IR/dialect/pattern-rewrite model, staged alongside the `mlir` donor (.atlas/provenance/donors/mlir.json) specifically because its Operation/Attribute/IRDL implementation is far more readable than MLIR's C++/TableGen originals and is a closer structural analog to what a from-scratch Rust ASIR implementation would look like (plain typed data structures + runtime-registered traits, no code-generation step required to get a working dialect).
not_a_runtime_dependency: Atlas does not and will not depend on xDSL as a runtime or build dependency for ASIR. This stage exists purely for architecture-education census; any adoption is a clean-room Rust reimplementation of studied ideas, never copied Python source.
